Per-position amino-acid frequency

Source: R/pepchem.R
aa_position_frequency.Rd

The position x residue frequency table a sequence logo draws, returned as data instead of a plot — the numeric complement to ggseqlogo_bylength() and the generalisation of anchor_information_content(), which collapses this same table to Shannon bits.

Usage

aa_position_frequency(
  sequences,
  length = NULL,
  positions = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  min_n = 10
)

Arguments

sequences

Character vector of peptide sequences.

length

Peptide length to restrict to, or NULL (default) for the modal length when positions is also NULL, and for "all lengths" when positions is given.

positions

Integer vector of positions to profile, or NULL (default) for all positions of the fixed length.

groups

Optional grouping vector, the same length as sequences.

min_n

Minimum number of usable sequences per group; a group below this is dropped, since its frequencies would be noise. Default 10.

Value

A long data frame with Group, Position (integer, as supplied, so negatives are preserved), PositionLabel (an ordered factor), AA, Count, n_Sequences and Frequency. Zero rows when nothing is usable.

Details

Two modes:

  • length given (or both length and positions NULL, which picks the modal length): only peptides of that length are used and every position 1..length is profiled. This is the mode for an anchor-motif heatmap.

  • positions given with length = NULL: peptides of all lengths are used and each position is resolved against that peptide's own length, so c(1, 2, -2, -1) profiles the two N-terminal and two C-terminal residues across a mixed-length set.

Negative positions count from the C-terminus (-1 is the last residue).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aa_position_frequency(pep_short$Sequence, groups = pep_short$Condition)
aa_position_frequency(pep_short$Sequence, positions = c(1, 2, -2, -1))
} # }
